changed_in.5.2: The list of search functions is called `package.searchers`; before this it was `package.loaders`. A searcher now hands back an extra value alongside the loader it found, and that value reaches the loader as a second argument after the module name. The record of what has been loaded is also written later than it was: earlier versions marked a module as being loaded before running it rather than after, so a load that failed part way through made every later call naming that module fail too, and a module that reached back to `require()` for itself while still running was stopped rather than run a second time.
changed_in.5.3: The C searcher builds the opening function's name differently for a module name carrying a version: the version is expected after the module name, and the first hyphen and everything following it are dropped, so `parcels.rates-v2` looks for `luaopen_parcels_rates`. Earlier versions dropped the part up to and including the first hyphen instead, which put the version in front.
changed_in.5.4: A second result comes back alongside the module's value — the loader data the searcher supplied, which for the searchers that read from disk is the path the module was found at. Nothing arrives there when the call found the module already loaded and did no loading of its own, which is how a caller tells the two cases apart. The `package.preload` searcher, which had supplied no such value at all, now supplies the string `":preload:"`.
